chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from a man, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man arrives from his journey at the time of salat (prayer). He said: if he does not fear the time passing, then let him complete; and if he fears the time passing, then let him shorten. And it is possible that completing is directed toward one upon whom the time entered while he was a traveler, then he entered upon his family, by way of recommendation and not obligation or mandatory requirement—this indicates that.

key_terms.خُرُوجَ الْوَقْتِ: the expiry of the prayer time
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ: let him perform the prayer in full
key_terms.وَقْتِ: the appointed time of the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: If a traveler reaches his family during the prayer time, should he pray in full or shortened form?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a traveler who arrives home during the time of salat (prayer). It distinguishes between completing and shortening the prayer based on fear of the prayer time expiring, and indicates that completion in some cases may be on the basis of recommendation rather than obligation.
